title: Knowledge Distillation: Soft Targets, Temperature, and the T² Factor
purpose: Explain how a teacher's logits become soft targets via a temperature-scaled softmax, how the soft-target cross-entropy is computed, and why the soft loss is multiplied by T² when combined with a hard-label loss.
scope: A single transfer example with small teacher and student logit vectors. We compute the temperature-scaled softmax distributions, the soft-target cross-entropy component, and the T²-scaled combination with a hard-label cross-entropy. No model training, no gradient derivation, no multi-example dataset.
intuition: A teacher's raw scores (logits) are turned into a probability distribution by a softmax. Raising the temperature T flattens that distribution, exposing relative similarities between classes that a hard label hides. The student is trained to match this soft distribution. Because the soft-target gradients shrink like 1/T², the soft loss is multiplied by T² so that changing T does not silently change the balance between soft and hard objectives.
learning_objectives: Compute temperature-scaled softmax distributions for teacher and student logits and describe how increasing T softens them.
Compute the soft-target cross-entropy component and the T²-scaled weighted combination with a hard-label cross-entropy.
prerequisites: Softmax as a normalized exponential of logits.
Cross-entropy H(p,q) = -Σ p_i ln q_i in nats.
assumptions: Teacher and student logit vectors are fixed small vectors for one transfer example; no training occurs.
The hard-label target is a one-hot distribution over the same classes, and the hard loss uses the student's T=1 softmax.
limitations: Only one transfer example is shown; real distillation averages over a transfer set.
The gradient-scaling argument for T² is stated from the paper but not derived here; we only apply the factor to the loss combination.
misconception: That temperature changes the teacher's knowledge or the student's logits themselves. Temperature only rescales the logits inside the softmax, changing the sharpness of the resulting distribution; the underlying logits are unchanged.
edge_cases: T = 1 makes the soft distribution identical to the ordinary softmax, so soft and hard targets use the same temperature.
Very large T drives the soft distribution toward uniform, so the soft cross-entropy approaches entropy of the teacher distribution and carries little class-specific signal.

inputs.name: teacher_logits
inputs.label: v (teacher logits)
inputs.meaning: Raw scores from the cumbersome teacher model for one transfer example, one entry per class.

inputs.name: student_logits
inputs.label: z (student logits)
inputs.meaning: Raw scores from the distilled student model for the same transfer example, one entry per class.

inputs.name: temperature
inputs.label: T
inputs.meaning: Softmax temperature used for distillation; higher T produces a softer distribution.

inputs.name: hard_target
inputs.label: y (hard label)
inputs.meaning: One-hot correct-label distribution over the same classes, used for the hard cross-entropy at T=1.

inputs.name: hard_weight
inputs.label: α (hard-loss weight)
inputs.meaning: Weight on the hard-label cross-entropy relative to the T²-scaled soft-target cross-entropy.

steps.name: teacher_soft
steps.label: p (teacher soft targets)
steps.meaning: Temperature-scaled softmax of the teacher logits, producing the soft target distribution the student is trained to match.

steps.name: student_soft
steps.label: q (student soft distribution at T)
steps.meaning: Temperature-scaled softmax of the student logits, using the same temperature as the teacher soft targets.

steps.name: soft_loss
steps.label: H(p, q) soft-target cross-entropy
steps.meaning: Cross-entropy between teacher soft targets and student soft distribution, computed at the distillation temperature.

steps.name: student_hard
steps.label: q₁ (student distribution at T=1)
steps.meaning: Student softmax at temperature 1, used for the hard-label cross-entropy.

steps.name: hard_loss
steps.label: H(y, q₁) hard-label cross-entropy
steps.meaning: Cross-entropy between the correct one-hot labels and the student distribution at T=1.

steps.name: total_loss
steps.label: L combined loss
steps.meaning: Weighted combination of the T²-scaled soft-target cross-entropy and the hard-label cross-entropy, preserving relative contributions as T changes.

visuals.question: How does increasing T flatten the teacher and student soft distributions?
How do the T²-scaled soft loss and the hard loss contribute to the total loss?

explorations.title: Temperature softens the targets
explorations.observe: teacher_soft and student_soft become flatter, soft_loss changes, and total_loss changes because the T² factor grows while the soft cross-entropy shrinks.
explorations.why: Dividing logits by a larger T compresses their differences before the softmax, so the exponential ratios move toward uniform. The soft cross-entropy then reflects a flatter target, and the T² multiplier compensates the 1/T² gradient scaling so the soft objective's relative weight stays comparable.

explorations.title: Hard-loss weight changes the balance
explorations.observe: soft_loss and hard_loss are unchanged from the baseline, but total_loss increases because the hard-label term is weighted more heavily.
explorations.why: The hard weight α multiplies only the hard cross-entropy, so raising α increases the hard objective's contribution without altering the soft-target cross-entropy or the temperature scaling.
